title: cfgaudit configuration (.cfgaudit.yml)
description: Configuration for cfgaudit, the security auditor for AI-agent configuration files. See https://github.com/cfgaudit/cfgaudit/blob/main/docs/usage.md#configuration-file-cfgaudityml

rules.description: Per-rule overrides: off to disable a rule, or a severity to change it. An ID no rule reports is only a warning, so a config written for a newer cfgaudit still loads.

strict.description: Treat warn findings as errors for the exit code.

no-exit-codes.description: Always exit 0 on a successful run (advisory mode for non-blocking CI).

exclude-paths.description: Path globs, relative to the scanned directory, whose findings are dropped. Supports *, ** and a trailing / for directory prefixes.

shellcheck.description: Run shellcheck on hook and helper commands (CFG045; needs the shellcheck binary).

shellcheck-exclude.description: ShellCheck codes CFG045 never reports, with or without the SC prefix.

content-paths.description: Globs naming files that agents read while they work but that are not instruction files, such as README.md. The high-precision instruction-content rules scan them too.

severity.description: error, warn or info, in any case.

policy.description: The organisation's permission policy, checked by CFG025 and CFG118.

require-deny.description: Claude Code permission entries that .claude/settings.json permissions.deny must cover, such as Bash(git push:*).

forbid-allow.description: Either Claude Code permission entries that permissions.allow must not grant, or agent-neutral commands and MCP tools that no agent's allow list may grant.

deny.description: Agent-neutral entries every agent in scope must deny, checked against each agent's committed permission file.

agents.description: The agents the agent-neutral policy applies to. Without it, every agent with configuration in the repository.

policyCommands.description: Shell commands, matched by word prefix: git push covers git push origin main.

policyPaths.description: Path globs relative to the repository, or to the home directory with a leading ~/.

policyMCPTools.description: server:tool pairs; the tool may be * or end in *.
